items.name: Destroyers USS Spruance, USS Michael Murphy return from extended combat deployments
items.summary: The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers USS Spruance and USS Michael Murphy returned to their homeports after lengthy deployments during the Iran war.
items.full_text:
Two Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers that played an integral role Middle East military operations during the Iran war returned to their homeports on Friday.

TheUSS Michael MurphyandUSS Spruancedocked at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii, and Naval Base San Diego, California, respectively. The Murphy deployed for 11 months while the Spruance deployed for 12.

“Leading the ship and crew has been the honor of a lifetime,” said Cmdr. Leigh R. Tate, commanding officer of Spruance. “Spruance sailors made a difference.”

Cmdr. David Nicolas, commanding officer of Michael Murphy, praised his crew for “defeating incoming air and surface threats” and “leading operations through contested choke points.”

The Spruance was deployed as part of the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group, while the Murphy operated as part of Carrier Strike Group 3 under Destroyer Squadron 21, sailing alongside the Spruance and Lincoln.

Both ships assisted with combat military operations during Operation Epic Fury and the Iran war, and helped enforce the maritime blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Spruance eliminated 12 unmanned aerial vehicles, four anti-ship cruise missiles and launched Tomahawk Land-Attack Cruise Missiles at Iranian targets.

In total, the destroyer logged 43 underway replenishments that successfully provided 8.6 million gallons of fuel.

It also helped facilitate 190 sorties and 1,150 flight hours for its embarked Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron Seven One.

Iranian government officials have claimed that munitions launched from the USS Spruance on Feb. 28 are responsible for a missile attack in Minab, Iran, that killed 156 civilians, 120 of whom were children.

Reuters first reported on March 5 that an initial, internal U.S. military investigation showed U.S. forces were likely responsible for the fatal strike in Minab on the opening day of the war with Iran.

Bloomberg on Oct. 15 reportedthat the Pentagon planned to hold its internal investigation until after midterms, despite various independent investigations alreadypointing to U.S. involvement in the strike.

On Friday, the Iranian governmentappearedto threaten the commander and executive officer of the ship in a social media post.

The Murphy defended 14 U.S. and allied nation vessels and transited through the Strait of Hormuz 12 times while facing surface, air and mine threats.

The ship netted 97,000 nautical miles, completed 43 replenishments-at-sea and eight combat in-port refuelings, and was responsible for the successful delivery of upwards of 10 million gallons of fuel for vessels.

The ship’s detached Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron Seven One component flew “330 sorties and over 900 mishap-free flight hours, including 273.4 combat flight hours,” the Navy said.

On Sept. 27, the Navy fired the Murphy’s commanding officer, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, due to a loss of confidence in her ability to command.

Service members aboard both ships were given the Presidential Unit Citation and the Combat Action Ribbon for their heroic efforts.

Riley Ceder is a reporter at Military Times, where he covers breaking news, criminal justice, investigations, and cyber. He previously worked as an investigative practicum student at The Washington Post, where he contributed to the Abused by the Badge investigation.
